newsitem.title: USA: W. Virginia seeks to avert welfare budget deficit.
newsitem.headline: W. Virginia seeks to avert welfare budget deficit.

text.p: West Virginia's social services chief will ask the legislature for added funding and legal changes to avert a $23 million budget deficit, the Daily Mail reported Friday.
Gretchen Lewis, state secretary of health and human resources, said she would make the request later this month at a special legislative session initially called to address flood relief.
She said the funding request would be less than the projected $23 million budget shortfall, though the exact amount had not been determined.
"I would expect more of a stopgap kind of measure, Lewis said.

The department's budget was $61 million for the year that will end June 30. It averted a $10 million deficit last year by tapping one-time sources of added federal and state funds. But those funds were not available this year, putting the department behind from the start.
Federal welfare reforms sliced another $5 million in revenues for the department, while state changes gave it responsibility for some programs previously funded via Medicaid, Lewis said.
Additionally, judges have ordered that a growing number of abused and neglected children be sent out of state to expensive residential treatment facilities.

Lewis said her department is working closely with groups developing residential treatment centers for juveniles in West Virginia. She said she would seek legislative changes allowing operators of those facilities to skip the lengthy and costly process of obtaining a state ruling that a need exists for the services.
